logline: A disgraced triple-board surgeon vanishes from Seoul's elite hospitals and resurfaces under an alias at a struggling rural trauma centre, where he mentors two younger doctors to put patients before institutional politics.

renewal.note: Three-season run concluded June 17, 2023. Seasons 2 and 3 were produced after the first season's exceptional broadcast ratings; no further seasons announced.

bollymeter.basis: Han Suk-kyu's Daesang-winning performance anchors a season that averaged 20.4 percent nationwide on SBS and peaked at 27.6 percent - exceptional figures that place it among the most-watched Korean medical dramas of its decade.

seasons.review_body: Romantic Doctor, Teacher Kim launched on SBS in November 2016 and averaged 20.4 percent nationwide - one of the strongest debut seasons for a Korean medical drama in years. The finale peaked at 27.6 percent, pulling audiences that typically gravitate toward prestige weekend dramas into a weekday slot. Han Suk-kyu's portrayal of Teacher Kim - a mentor figure who uses abrasiveness as a form of radical honesty - won the SBS Drama Awards Grand Prize (Daesang) and the ABU Grand Prize in 2017. Director Yoo In-shik won the Baeksang Arts Best Director award. Critics and viewers aligned: the show works because Kim Sa-bu's philosophy is embodied rather than lectured, and the Doldam Hospital setting creates genuine stakes by placing idealism against resource scarcity rather than just professional rivalry.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Romantic Doctor, Teacher Kim Season 1 Episode 1 aired November 7, 2016 on SBS as the premiere of a 20-episode series that averaged 20.4 percent nationwide and peaked at 27.6 percent for its finale. IMDb audience scored the series 8.4. Director Yoo In-shik won the Baeksang Arts Best Director award; Han Suk-kyu's performance won the SBS Drama Awards Daesang and the ABU Grand Prize 2017. The premiere establishes the Doldam Hospital setting in a single shift: underfunded, chaotic, staffed by people who either cannot or will not function in Seoul's prestige hospital system. Han Suk-kyu's Kim Sa-bu appears mid-episode and the register changes immediately - he is abrasive where the genre delivers warmth, demanding where it nurtures, and the abrasiveness is framed from the first scene as a form of radical honesty about what medicine at the margins requires. The debut episode's first emergency surgery, performed in conditions unthinkable at a Seoul teaching hospital, announces the show's argument without a single line of thesis dialogue.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the rule of Doldam Hospital in a single shift: chaotic, underfunded, staffed by people who either cannot or will not operate in the prestige system. Han Suk-kyu appears mid-episode and the register changes immediately - his Teacher Kim is not warm or welcoming, and that refusal to coddle is what makes the show feel different from the genre default.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Kim Sa-bu's first surgical intervention - performed in conditions that would be unthinkable at Seoul's elite hospitals, executed with complete confidence.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 20
episode_reviews.review_body: Romantic Doctor, Teacher Kim Season 1 Episode 20 aired January 16, 2017 on SBS as the finale of the 20-episode first season that averaged 20.4 percent nationwide. The finale peaked at 27.6 percent, reflecting an audience fully committed to the characters and the Doldam Hospital philosophy. IMDb audience scored the series 8.4; Han Suk-kyu's performance won the SBS Drama Awards Daesang and the ABU Grand Prize 2017. The finale closes every character arc with discipline the genre rarely manages: the younger doctors' growth is measured against their starting points rather than an idealised endpoint, and Teacher Kim's backstory receives resolution that does not make him sentimental. The central speech about what it means to be a good doctor is the moment the season's accumulated argument is delivered in explicit form - and it lands because twenty episodes of demonstrated practice give the words weight that a first-episode declaration would not.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale closes every character arc with discipline: the younger doctors' growth is measured against where they started rather than against an idealised endpoint, and Teacher Kim's backstory is resolved without making him sentimental. The 27.6 percent broadcast rating reflects an audience that had fully committed to the show's unglamorous vision of medicine.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Kim Sa-bu explains what it actually means to be a good doctor - a speech that earned the show its reputation for dialogue with genuine weight.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 averaged 18.3 percent with a 25.4 percent finale - strong numbers that indicate the audience transferred loyalty intact across a three-year gap, though some critics noted diminishing freshness in the formula.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 returned in January 2020, three years after the first season's exceptional run, with a new resident pair replacing the original younger doctors. The nationwide average of 18.3 percent and a finale at 25.4 percent demonstrated the franchise's sustained audience pull. Ahn Hyo-seop and Lee Sung-kyung took the younger lead roles and drew their own critical attention for chemistry that mirrored the first season's dynamic without repeating it. The Doldam Hospital formula - chaotic emergency, philosophical confrontation with Kim Sa-bu, resolution under pressure - ran to a second iteration with diminished freshness but undiminished craft. Han Suk-kyu's continued command of the mentor role remained the season's strongest asset.
seasons.season_over_season: Swaps the resident pair while retaining Han Suk-kyu as the constant; ratings came in slightly below Season 1's peak but above most contemporaries, confirming the formula holds.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 averaged 13.7 percent nationwide - respectable but below the franchise's prior floors - suggesting the show retained its core audience while failing to grow beyond it in the more competitive 2023 landscape.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 aired April to June 2023 and averaged 13.7 percent nationwide, peaking at 16.8 percent in the finale. The decline relative to the first two seasons reflects both the maturation of the streaming landscape - where a SBS drama now competes against global platforms for the same viewing time - and a familiar pattern for franchise third seasons. Han Suk-kyu returned for a third outing as Kim Sa-bu, and the Doldam Hospital premise was refreshed with new resident characters. Critical reception remained positive in tone if less effusive: the show knew what it was and delivered it competently, even if the sense of discovery that made Season 1 exceptional was long gone.
seasons.season_over_season: Lowest ratings of the three-season run but retains the core Doldam formula; Han Suk-kyu's performance remains the franchise's load-bearing element through a third rotation of junior characters.
